item.title: The Clown Who Returned To Marry The Victim’s Husband
item.description: In 1990, a clown carrying flowers and balloons shot Marlene Warren at her Florida home. More than three decades later, Sheila Keen-Warren pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. She had been suspected for years and later married Marlene’s widower, Michael Warren.

item.title: The Murder Case That Shocked Even Seasoned Prosecutors
item.description: In 1991, Omaima Nelson killed her newlywed husband, William, in their Costa Mesa apartment. She claimed self-defense after years of abuse, but a jury convicted her of second-degree murder in 1993. She was sentenced to 27 years to life and denied parole in 2011.

item.title: Their First Date Was The Last Time She Came Home
item.description: Nineteen-year-old Sade Robinson disappeared after meeting Maxwell Anderson for a first date in Milwaukee in April 2024. Anderson was convicted of first-degree intentional homicide and other charges in 2025 and sentenced to life in prison without parole.

item.title: The Six Year Old Who Vanished Without A Trace
item.description: Mary Boyle disappeared near her grandparents’ home in County Donegal on March 18, 1977, after following her uncle partway toward a nearby house. Despite repeated searches, reviews and an arrest decades later, Mary has never been found and the investigation remains open.

item.title: Her Death Looked Like Suicide Until One Clue
item.description: Actress and filmmaker Adrienne Shelly was found hanging in her Manhattan apartment in 2006, initially appearing to have died by suicide. A sneaker print at the scene led detectives to construction worker Diego Pillco, who later pleaded guilty to manslaughter and admitted staging her death to look like suicide.

item.title: The Lies That Became A Lasting Part Of Casey Anthony’s Case
item.description: Casey Anthony was acquitted of murdering her daughter Caylee in 2011 but convicted of lying to investigators about her disappearance. An appeals court later overturned two of those four convictions, leaving two in place.

item.title: The Wellness Empire Built On A Fake Cancer Story
item.description: Belle Gibson built a successful wellness brand around claims that she had survived brain cancer through alternative treatments. She later admitted she never had cancer, and Australia’s Federal Court found she had engaged in misleading conduct and ordered her to pay $410,000 in penalties.

item.title: He Turned His Slasher Fantasy Into A Killing Spree
item.description: Daniel Gonzalez, who called himself a horror fan, murdered four strangers and attempted to kill two others during a 2004 rampage in England. He told police he wanted to experience being like Freddy Krueger for a day. Gonzalez was convicted of murder and sentenced to life without release.

item.title: Her Boyfriend’s Brother Found Her Body
item.description: Rebecca Zahau was found hanging from a balcony at her boyfriend’s Coronado mansion in 2011, days after his young son suffered a fatal fall. Authorities ruled her death a suicide, but a civil jury later found Adam Shacknai, who discovered her body, liable for her death.

item.title: Did Sarah Boone Know She Was Leaving Him To Die?
item.description: Sarah Boone said Jorge Torres climbed into a suitcase during a drunken game of hide-and-seek and that she fell asleep, forgetting he was inside. Phone videos showed Torres pleading for help, and Boone was later convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison.
